title: incident report: fail-open drain policy triggered cascading variant surge
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: On 2026-02-24 an interaction between the region drain controller and the routing policy caused simultaneous drain decisions across two regions. The routing control plane defaulted to a fail-open path which routed large volumes to lower-capacity variant models and cross-region endpoints, producing a cascading fallback surge, higher tail latency, and increased 5xx rates for hosted customers for ~47 minutes.
impact: ~47 minutes of elevated 5xx and p99 latency for ~12% of request volume in NA/EU regions; several high-traffic customers observed increased error rates and cost spike due to repeated fallback to larger token-count retries.
detection: On-call alerts fired for region-aggregate 5xx rate and p99 latency at 2026-02-24T13:04Z. SRE runbooks triggered automated dashboard runbooks and paging. Engineers noticed an unusual correlation between 'drain-active' flags and cross-region egress during the first 6 minutes of the incident.
timeline: 2026-02-24T12:58Z - small heartbeat gap observed in region-eu-1; drain-controller evaluated node health with smoothing window of 10s
2026-02-24T13:01Z - drain-controller issued drain tokens for eu-1 and na-2 within a 30s window due to concurrent degraded telemetry
2026-02-24T13:02Z - routing control plane entered 'fail-open' mode because quorum check failed; requests were allowed to route to compatible variants and remote tiers
2026-02-24T13:03Z - sudden increase in cross-region routing and swaps to quantized low-memory variants observed; p95/p99 latency and 5xx began rising
2026-02-24T13:04Z - on-call alerted; SRE started mitigation steps
2026-02-24T13:12Z - emergency runbook: rollback fail-open flag and apply temporary conservative routing policy (no cross-region egress unless explicit override)
2026-02-24T13:20Z - traffic shifted back to primary regions and model variants; 5xx and tail latency began to decline
2026-02-24T13:45Z - metrics returned to baseline; post-incident monitoring continued until 14:30Z
root_cause: Two contributing bugs: (1) drain-controller's smoothing window was set too small and had an edge-case where simultaneous short telemetry gaps across two regions caused concurrent drains; (2) the routing control plane's fail-open behavior lacked a minimum-quorum check and allowed wide cross-region egress and automatic variant swapping under capacity pressure, amplifying the impact.
mitigation_steps_taken: Immediate: rolled back the fail-open routing flag and applied conservative egress gating (no cross-region egress without explicit override)
Immediate: paused automatic variant swaps for affected model families for 30 minutes
Hotfix: increased drain-controller smoothing window from 10s to 45s to prevent short transient dual-drain decisions
Hotfix: added a quorum requirement to the routing controller so fail-open only occurs when at most one region is draining
Communication: customer-facing incident note posted and SRE notified affected customers directly
postmortem_notes: The interaction of two defensive systems (drain-controller and fail-open routing) produced a defensive amplification rather than graceful degradation. We accidentally optimized for availability under single-region failure and not for correlated short-lived telemetry gaps across regions. The conservative fix is to treat simultaneous small drains as a soft-degrade state rather than immediate full drain and to make fail-open decisions rely on a quorum and cost/latency heuristics.
follow_up_actions: ENG-41710 - routing: add routing-simulator test coverage for simultaneous drain scenarios (assigned Mei Chen)
ENG-41890 - drain-controller: audit all smoothing windows and implement adaptive smoothing (assigned Rafael Torres)
ENG-41921 - routing: implement cost-aware fallback throttling to limit repeated variant swaps (assigned Liam O'Connor)
DOCS-220 - Update on-call runbooks to include 'simultaneous drain' playbook and cross-checks with capacity telemetry (assigned Aisha Patel)
SLO-clarify - Review SLOs around cross-region egress and ambiguity in fail-open tolerances (platform goals team)
Add a regression test in CI that replays the production trace that triggered the event
decisions_made: Do not remove fail-open permanently; instead require quorum and latency/cost thresholds before allowing it
Increase smoothing windows for drain signals and add an adaptive decay based on historical heartbeat variance
Pause automatic variant swaps for model families flagged as sensitive to quantization before they are re-enabled behind stricter throttling
open_questions: What is the correct quorum definition across multi-AZ and multi-region clusters when evaluating drain decisions?
How should routing prioritize unit-cost vs latency when a degraded region forces fallback to more expensive cross-region capacity?
Do we need a centralized 'drain arbitration' service to avoid independent controllers making conflicting drain decisions?
comments: 2026-02-24 13:10 - Mei Chen: started binary-searching control plane flag that enables fail-open behavior. Found that toggling 'routing.fail_open.enable' stabilized traffic immediately.
2026-02-24 13:18 - Rafael Torres: applied temporary conservative egress gating; monitoring shows p99 improved by ~40% compared to peak
2026-02-25 09:00 - Product Review: PD reviewed customer impact and asked for prioritized follow-ups for high-visibility customers
2026-02-27 16:45 - Security Review: no secrets or policy violations found; KMS unaffected
2026-03-01 11:20 - Review Meeting: agreed on quorum-based fail-open and adaptive smoothing as primary mitigation; assigned actions and owners
conclusion: This incident demonstrates that defensive mechanisms can interact in non-obvious ways. We have implemented both immediate controls and medium-term engineering work to reduce the chance of recurrence. The prioritized follow-ups will be tracked under the smart-routing-stability project and reviewed in the next platform reliability review.
